name: Active listening
description: Understand another person’s point before responding by giving attention, asking clarifying questions and checking your interpretation.

levels.name: Listen without rushing
levels.completion_criterion: In a short conversation, let the other person finish and restate their main point in your own words.
levels.can_do: Give sustained attention and paraphrase a speaker’s main point.

levels.name: Clarify and check
levels.completion_criterion: Ask at least two relevant follow-up questions and confirm whether your summary is accurate.
levels.can_do: Use open questions and check understanding rather than assuming.

levels.name: Track a complex conversation
levels.completion_criterion: Summarise the different concerns in a longer conversation and distinguish what was said from your interpretation.
levels.can_do: Listen across several points, reflect them fairly and identify unresolved questions.

emoji_rationale: The ear represents attention to another person before responding.

name: Nonverbal communication
description: Notice and use visible and vocal cues while remembering that gestures and expressions are context-dependent and do not reliably reveal a person’s thoughts by themselves.

levels.name: Notice observable cues
levels.completion_criterion: Describe two observable cues in a short interaction without claiming to know the person’s hidden intent.
levels.can_do: Notice posture, gesture, facial expression and conversational timing as observations.

levels.name: Match cues to context
levels.completion_criterion: Practise using a suitable posture, eye contact where culturally comfortable, and tone for two different settings.
levels.can_do: Adapt your own nonverbal communication to context while avoiding assumptions.

levels.name: Check interpretations
levels.completion_criterion: When a cue is ambiguous, ask a respectful clarifying question and revise your interpretation based on the response.
levels.can_do: Treat nonverbal cues as tentative information and verify meaning with the person.

emoji_rationale: Eyes represent attention to facial expression, gestures and context.

name: Constructive conflict resolution
description: Clarify disagreements by listening to the people involved, identifying the disputed issue and agreeing on a practical next step when possible.

levels.name: Separate positions
levels.completion_criterion: Describe the disagreement in neutral language and state each side’s concern without assigning blame.
levels.can_do: Identify the issue and represent opposing views fairly.

levels.name: Explore options
levels.completion_criterion: Ask each party what outcome matters and suggest at least two possible next steps.
levels.can_do: Move from competing positions to possible solutions.

levels.name: Agree and review
levels.completion_criterion: Record a mutually accepted action, who will do it and when to revisit whether it worked.
levels.can_do: Help turn a discussion into a clear agreement and follow-up.

emoji_rationale: The dove signals de-escalation and constructive resolution.
safety_notes: For threatening, abusive or coercive situations, prioritise safety and seek appropriate help; do not treat every conflict as safe to mediate.

name: Explain information clearly
description: Make information understandable to another person by identifying the main point, choosing relevant details and checking what the listener needs clarified.

levels.name: State the main point
levels.completion_criterion: Explain a familiar idea in a few sentences and ask the listener to say what they understood.
levels.can_do: Find the central message and express it in plain language.

levels.name: Adapt the explanation
levels.completion_criterion: Explain the same idea to two audiences using different examples or levels of detail.
levels.can_do: Choose relevant wording and examples for the listener’s background.

levels.name: Handle questions and uncertainty
levels.completion_criterion: Answer follow-up questions, separate facts from assumptions and say what you do not know.
levels.can_do: Explain complex information without overstating certainty.

emoji_rationale: A speech bubble represents making information understandable in conversation.

name: Public speaking and audience adaptation
description: Prepare and deliver a short talk with a clear structure, suitable examples and language adapted to the audience.

levels.name: Deliver a short talk
levels.completion_criterion: Give a one-minute explanation with a clear opening, main point and closing.
levels.can_do: Speak from a simple plan rather than reading every sentence.

levels.name: Adapt to the audience
levels.completion_criterion: Deliver the same topic to two different audiences, changing the examples or terminology appropriately.
levels.can_do: Adjust structure and detail to the audience and occasion.

levels.name: Respond and recover
levels.completion_criterion: Give a three-to-five-minute talk and respond to a question while keeping the central message clear.
levels.can_do: Maintain structure and recover calmly when interrupted or asked to clarify.

emoji_rationale: A microphone represents speaking to a group.

name: Everyday foreign-language conversation
description: Build practical conversational ability in another language, from prepared exchanges to maintaining a conversation and repairing misunderstandings.

levels.name: Manage a simple exchange
levels.completion_criterion: Introduce yourself and complete a short prepared exchange on a familiar topic.
levels.can_do: Use basic phrases and ask for repetition when needed.

levels.name: Sustain a conversation
levels.completion_criterion: Hold a short conversation on a familiar subject, asking follow-up questions without relying entirely on a script.
levels.can_do: Connect sentences and respond to what the other person says.

levels.name: Repair misunderstandings
levels.completion_criterion: Continue an unscripted conversation by paraphrasing, requesting clarification and explaining when a word is missing.
levels.can_do: Use repair strategies to keep communication going despite gaps.

emoji_rationale: The globe represents communicating across languages.
safety_notes: Use this skill for practice, not as evidence of professional translation competence or readiness for high-stakes interpretation.

name: Informal spoken interpreting
description: Convey the meaning of a short spoken message between two languages while preserving the speaker’s intent and acknowledging uncertainty.

levels.name: Convey a short message
levels.completion_criterion: In a low-stakes practice exercise, relay a short sentence in the other language without adding opinions.
levels.can_do: Carry the basic meaning across languages.

levels.name: Preserve details
levels.completion_criterion: Interpret a short multi-sentence exchange and ask for repetition when a name, number or phrase is unclear.
levels.can_do: Preserve key details and signal uncertainty rather than guessing.

levels.name: Handle nuance transparently
levels.completion_criterion: Interpret a longer low-stakes exchange, clarify ambiguous wording and distinguish the speaker’s words from your own explanation.
levels.can_do: Manage turn-taking and acknowledge limits of understanding.

emoji_rationale: The speech bubble represents conveying a spoken message between people.
safety_notes: Not for medical, legal, emergency or other high-stakes interpreting. Use a qualified interpreter for consequential decisions.

name: Translate short texts faithfully
description: Translate short written messages between languages while preserving meaning, tone and important details instead of translating word for word without context.

levels.name: Translate a short message
levels.completion_criterion: Translate a short everyday message and compare names, numbers and the central meaning against the original.
levels.can_do: Produce a readable translation of simple content.

levels.name: Preserve tone and nuance
levels.completion_criterion: Translate a longer passage, checking idioms and register instead of mapping each word mechanically.
levels.can_do: Choose expressions appropriate to context and audience.

levels.name: Review and annotate uncertainty
levels.completion_criterion: Revise a translation against the original and flag unresolved ambiguity rather than inventing a meaning.
levels.can_do: Explain consequential translation choices and recognise limits.

emoji_rationale: Letters represent written language and meaning transfer.
safety_notes: Do not use informal practice as a substitute for certified translation where legal or official requirements apply.

name: Write concisely
description: Make writing direct and readable by removing repetition, vague phrasing and words that do not contribute to the intended meaning.

levels.name: Remove obvious padding
levels.completion_criterion: Revise a short paragraph by deleting repetition while preserving its meaning.
levels.can_do: Recognise unnecessary words and redundant phrases.

levels.name: Choose precise wording
levels.completion_criterion: Rewrite a wordy passage with more specific verbs and nouns, then check that no key detail was lost.
levels.can_do: Improve directness without reducing accuracy.

levels.name: Edit for purpose
levels.completion_criterion: Produce a concise version for a specific reader and explain which details were kept, moved or removed.
levels.can_do: Balance brevity with the information the reader needs.

emoji_rationale: Scissors represent trimming words that do not serve the message.

name: Outline and structure a piece of writing
description: Organise ideas into a logical sequence before drafting, grouping related points and showing how the parts support the purpose.

levels.name: Make a simple outline
levels.completion_criterion: Create a title, purpose and ordered list of main points before writing a short piece.
levels.can_do: Turn unstructured ideas into a basic plan.

levels.name: Group and order ideas
levels.completion_criterion: Group related points, remove or relocate tangents and add supporting subpoints.
levels.can_do: Build a logical sequence that serves the writing purpose.

levels.name: Use structure to guide a longer piece
levels.completion_criterion: Create a hierarchical outline for a multi-section piece and explain how each section supports the main claim or story.
levels.can_do: Plan boundaries, hierarchy and progression before drafting.

emoji_rationale: A filing box represents grouping and ordering ideas before drafting.

name: Write clear, coherent paragraphs
description: Develop paragraphs around a central idea, using relevant supporting material and transitions that help a reader follow the reasoning.

levels.name: Keep one focus
levels.completion_criterion: Write a paragraph in which each sentence supports one identifiable main idea.
levels.can_do: Recognise and maintain paragraph unity.

levels.name: Develop the idea
levels.completion_criterion: Support the main point with relevant explanation, evidence or an example and connect sentences clearly.
levels.can_do: Develop a complete, coherent paragraph.

levels.name: Check flow across paragraphs
levels.completion_criterion: Revise a multi-paragraph piece so each paragraph has a clear role and transitions connect the sequence.
levels.can_do: Build continuity without making every paragraph follow a rigid template.

emoji_rationale: Bricks represent paragraphs that form a coherent larger structure.

name: Build a reasoned written argument
description: State a clear claim, support it with relevant reasons or evidence, and address objections without confusing assertion with proof.

levels.name: State a clear claim
levels.completion_criterion: Write a thesis or central claim that can be understood and discussed, rather than a broad topic label.
levels.can_do: Distinguish a claim from a subject area.

levels.name: Support the claim
levels.completion_criterion: Write a short argument with at least two relevant reasons or pieces of evidence and explain how they support the claim.
levels.can_do: Connect evidence and reasoning to a central position.

levels.name: Address a reasonable objection
levels.completion_criterion: Revise the argument to acknowledge a plausible counterpoint and explain why the claim still holds or needs narrowing.
levels.can_do: Build a fair, qualified argument rather than ignoring alternatives.

emoji_rationale: The megaphone represents making a claim and supporting it clearly.

name: Map an argument visually
description: Represent a claim, its supporting reasons and relevant objections in a visual structure that makes the logic easier to inspect.

levels.name: Map the basic structure
levels.completion_criterion: Draw one claim and connect it to two reasons that support it.
levels.can_do: Represent a simple argument as linked statements.

levels.name: Separate evidence and inference
levels.completion_criterion: Label supporting evidence and the reasoning that links it to the claim; distinguish objections from supporting reasons.
levels.can_do: Make the structure and role of each statement explicit.

levels.name: Compare competing arguments
levels.completion_criterion: Map a claim and a counterclaim, identify unsupported links and revise the diagram after checking the text.
levels.can_do: Use a diagram to examine rather than merely decorate an argument.

emoji_rationale: A web-like diagram represents connected claims and reasons.

name: Proofread and track recurring writing errors
description: Review a finished draft for spelling, punctuation, grammar and obvious clarity problems using a consistent checking method.

levels.name: Check a short draft
levels.completion_criterion: Find and correct obvious spelling, punctuation and typographical errors in a short text.
levels.can_do: Perform a deliberate final pass rather than relying on memory.

levels.name: Use a repeatable checklist
levels.completion_criterion: Proofread a longer text using separate passes for different error types and record recurring mistakes.
levels.can_do: Apply a systematic method to reduce missed errors.

levels.name: Proofread for reader impact
levels.completion_criterion: Read a final draft aloud or in a different format, fix awkward or unclear passages and verify the corrections.
levels.can_do: Notice problems that are easy to miss when reading as the author.

emoji_rationale: A sponge represents cleaning up a finished draft.

name: Revise writing for coherence
description: Improve an existing draft by checking its central point, order, relevance and transitions before polishing sentence-level details.

levels.name: Check what each paragraph does
levels.completion_criterion: Write a short margin label for each paragraph and identify places where the sequence is confusing or repetitive.
levels.can_do: Review a draft’s structure from the reader’s point of view.

levels.name: Reorder and connect
levels.completion_criterion: Move or combine paragraphs and improve transitions so that ideas follow a clear sequence.
levels.can_do: Revise the flow of ideas rather than only correcting grammar.

levels.name: Make a purposeful second draft
levels.completion_criterion: Compare the revised draft with the original and explain how each major change improves logic, relevance or reader understanding.
levels.can_do: Make structural revisions intentionally and evaluate their effect.

emoji_rationale: A needle represents joining parts of a draft into a coherent whole.

name: Write effective emails
description: Write clear, appropriate email messages with a useful subject line, a concise body, a suitable tone and a clear next step.

levels.name: Compose a clear email
levels.completion_criterion: Write a short email with a meaningful subject, greeting, clear request or message and appropriate closing.
levels.can_do: Structure an email so the recipient can quickly understand its purpose.

levels.name: Match tone and detail
levels.completion_criterion: Adjust formality and context for a familiar person versus an unfamiliar or professional recipient.
levels.can_do: Choose a suitable tone and include only useful details.

levels.name: Manage a thread responsibly
levels.completion_criterion: Write a follow-up that quotes only relevant context, answers questions clearly and avoids sharing sensitive information unnecessarily.
levels.can_do: Maintain clarity and privacy across an email exchange.

emoji_rationale: The envelope represents everyday written communication.
safety_notes: Avoid including passwords, payment credentials or unnecessarily sensitive personal information in ordinary email.

name: Give and use constructive writing feedback
description: Review another person’s writing against its purpose, describe specific issues respectfully, and turn feedback into an actionable revision plan.

levels.name: Comment on one specific point
levels.completion_criterion: Give feedback on one clear strength and one concrete improvement, referring to the relevant passage.
levels.can_do: Describe the text and its effect rather than judging the writer.

levels.name: Prioritise feedback
levels.completion_criterion: Separate structure and argument issues from sentence-level corrections and explain which change matters most.
levels.can_do: Organise review comments by importance and scope.

levels.name: Turn feedback into a revision plan
levels.completion_criterion: Create a list of changes, decide which suggestions to apply and explain why some feedback may not fit the purpose.
levels.can_do: Use feedback thoughtfully without surrendering authorship.

emoji_rationale: A note sheet represents specific, actionable review comments.

name: Practise recalling information from memory
description: Strengthen study routines by attempting to recall material before checking notes, then using errors to guide the next review.

levels.name: Recall before checking
levels.completion_criterion: After studying a short topic, answer a few questions from memory before reopening the material.
levels.can_do: Attempt retrieval instead of only rereading.

levels.name: Check and correct
levels.completion_criterion: Compare answers with reliable notes and correct gaps or misconceptions.
levels.can_do: Use feedback from recall attempts to identify what needs review.

levels.name: Build a reusable recall set
levels.completion_criterion: Create and reuse questions across a topic, mixing factual recall with explanation and application.
levels.can_do: Use retrieval to monitor learning and guide further study.

emoji_rationale: The brain represents recalling information without looking at the answer.

name: Space practice over time
description: Plan multiple learning sessions separated by intervals rather than concentrating all review into one sitting.

levels.name: Plan more than one session
levels.completion_criterion: Schedule at least two reviews on different days instead of doing the entire review at once.
levels.can_do: Distribute practice over time.

levels.name: Review after a gap
levels.completion_criterion: Return to material after an interval and attempt recall before checking notes.
levels.can_do: Combine spacing with an active check of what remains accessible.

levels.name: Adjust the plan from results
levels.completion_criterion: Use recall results to decide which topics need earlier review and which can wait longer.
levels.can_do: Adapt spacing to the difficulty of the material and your actual recall.

emoji_rationale: A calendar represents practice distributed over time.

name: Interleave similar types of practice
description: Alternate related problem types or concepts so you practise deciding which approach fits each case rather than repeating only one type at a time.

levels.name: Mix two related types
levels.completion_criterion: Practise a small set of two related task types in alternating order.
levels.can_do: Recognise which type of task you are facing.

levels.name: Choose the method before solving
levels.completion_criterion: Mix several similar-looking tasks and select the method for each before checking the result.
levels.can_do: Discriminate among approaches rather than following a repeated pattern.

levels.name: Review choice errors
levels.completion_criterion: Record why the wrong method was selected and adapt the next mixed set to address that confusion.
levels.can_do: Use errors to improve selection among related methods.

emoji_rationale: Crossing paths represent alternating related practice types.

name: Combine words and visuals when learning
description: Pair a concise verbal explanation with a relevant diagram, timeline or sketch so that both express the same idea accurately.

levels.name: Pair a term with a simple visual
levels.completion_criterion: Create a small labelled sketch or diagram beside a short written explanation.
levels.can_do: Represent one concept verbally and visually.

levels.name: Choose the right visual structure
levels.completion_criterion: Use a timeline, flow diagram or comparison table appropriate to the relationship being explained.
levels.can_do: Select visuals that match the structure of the information.

levels.name: Check both representations
levels.completion_criterion: Explain the concept using the visual, then verify that no important relationship or qualification is missing.
levels.can_do: Use words and visuals as complementary representations, not decoration.

emoji_rationale: A picture frame represents using a visual alongside words.

name: Connect new ideas to what you already know
description: Deepen understanding by asking why or how a claim works and linking it to relevant prior knowledge while distinguishing evidence from speculation.

levels.name: Ask why or how
levels.completion_criterion: For a concept, write one why-question and answer it in your own words using the material you studied.
levels.can_do: Move beyond repeating a definition.

levels.name: Connect two concepts
levels.completion_criterion: Explain how a new idea relates to a familiar example or concept and where the comparison breaks down.
levels.can_do: Build and test meaningful connections.

levels.name: Explain the limits of an analogy
levels.completion_criterion: Give an explanation with a supporting example and name a condition where the example or analogy would mislead.
levels.can_do: Use elaboration carefully without treating every association as evidence.

emoji_rationale: A light bulb represents making meaningful connections between ideas.

name: Learn concepts through concrete examples
description: Make abstract ideas easier to understand by generating, comparing and checking specific examples and counterexamples.

levels.name: Find one suitable example
levels.completion_criterion: Give a specific example of a concept and explain which features make it fit.
levels.can_do: Connect an abstract definition to a concrete case.

levels.name: Compare examples
levels.completion_criterion: Compare two cases and identify which features are essential and which are incidental.
levels.can_do: Recognise the concept across different examples.

levels.name: Use a counterexample
levels.completion_criterion: Create or identify a nearby case that does not fit, and explain the distinguishing feature.
levels.can_do: Clarify the boundaries of a concept rather than memorising a single example.

emoji_rationale: A test tube represents trying a concrete illustration of an idea.

name: Evaluate claims and evidence
description: Assess the support for a claim by distinguishing facts, interpretations and assumptions, checking sources and considering reasonable alternatives.

levels.name: Separate claim from evidence
levels.completion_criterion: Read a short argument and mark its main claim and at least one supporting reason.
levels.can_do: Identify what is asserted and what support is offered.

levels.name: Check evidence quality
levels.completion_criterion: Compare the claim with its source, identify an assumption and look for a plausible alternative explanation.
levels.can_do: Evaluate relevance and limits of evidence.

levels.name: Write a qualified conclusion
levels.completion_criterion: Summarise what the available evidence supports, what remains uncertain and what additional evidence would change your view.
levels.can_do: Make a reasoned conclusion without overstating certainty.

emoji_rationale: The monocle face represents close examination rather than instant acceptance.

name: Solve everyday problems systematically
description: Define a problem, identify constraints, compare options, try a suitable solution and review the result.

levels.name: Define the problem
levels.completion_criterion: State the problem, desired outcome and one or two constraints without jumping straight to a solution.
levels.can_do: Separate the actual issue from symptoms or assumptions.

levels.name: Compare options
levels.completion_criterion: List at least two feasible approaches, compare their trade-offs and select one for a small test.
levels.can_do: Choose a solution using explicit criteria.

levels.name: Review the result
levels.completion_criterion: Check whether the trial met the goal, explain what caused the result and adjust the next action.
levels.can_do: Use outcomes to refine a solution rather than repeating it blindly.

emoji_rationale: The abacus represents breaking a problem into manageable parts.

name: Solve crosswords systematically
description: Use clue wording, crossings and theme clues to solve a crossword, keeping uncertain answers provisional until checked.

levels.name: Use crossings
levels.completion_criterion: Solve straightforward clues and use crossing letters to test uncertain entries.
levels.can_do: Combine clue meaning with intersecting answers.

levels.name: Work with wordplay
levels.completion_criterion: Recognise synonyms, abbreviations, wordplay or multiple meanings when simple definition clues are not enough.
levels.can_do: Apply different clue-solving approaches.

levels.name: Check the whole grid
levels.completion_criterion: Review theme relationships and crossing consistency, revising entries that conflict with the grid.
levels.can_do: Use overall consistency to resolve uncertain answers.

emoji_rationale: Letters represent word clues and crossing answers.

name: Solve Sudoku puzzles with logical elimination
description: Solve number-placement puzzles by tracking constraints and using explicit logical deductions rather than guessing.

levels.name: Use row, column and box constraints
levels.completion_criterion: Complete simple placements by checking which digits are missing from a row, column or box.
levels.can_do: Apply the core Sudoku constraints consistently.

levels.name: Use candidate notes
levels.completion_criterion: Record possible digits in empty cells and eliminate candidates using visible constraints.
levels.can_do: Track possibilities to avoid repeated guessing.

levels.name: Explain a deduction
levels.completion_criterion: Solve a harder section by identifying a logical relationship that removes candidates, and explain why it must hold.
levels.can_do: Use and verify a chain of logical deductions.

emoji_rationale: Digits represent number-placement logic.

name: Solve jigsaw puzzles strategically
description: Organise pieces and use shape, colour, pattern and image structure to assemble a jigsaw without relying on random placement alone.

levels.name: Build a reliable start
levels.completion_criterion: Separate edge pieces and organise a few obvious colour or pattern groups before assembling.
levels.can_do: Create a manageable starting structure.

levels.name: Assemble sections
levels.completion_criterion: Complete distinct regions using shape and image clues, then connect the regions.
levels.can_do: Use local patterns while keeping the overall image in mind.

levels.name: Manage ambiguous pieces
levels.completion_criterion: Compare shape, colour and neighbouring image details to resolve difficult placements and revise incorrect sections.
levels.can_do: Combine multiple clues and backtrack methodically.

emoji_rationale: A puzzle piece directly represents the activity.

name: Read topographic maps and relate them to terrain
description: Interpret map symbols, scale, contours and visible landmarks to understand how a mapped area corresponds to real terrain.

levels.name: Identify map features
levels.completion_criterion: Use the legend to identify several mapped features and locate them on a familiar, low-risk route.
levels.can_do: Read common symbols and connect them to visible landmarks.

levels.name: Interpret scale and contours
levels.completion_criterion: Estimate a distance from the map scale and explain what contour spacing suggests about the shape or steepness of terrain.
levels.can_do: Use scale and contours to understand mapped distances and relief.

levels.name: Relate map to ground
levels.completion_criterion: On a simple marked route, match at least three terrain features to the map and explain where uncertainty remains.
levels.can_do: Combine symbols, relief and landmarks when reading unfamiliar terrain.

emoji_rationale: A map represents the skill of reading symbols and terrain together.
safety_notes: Practise first on a familiar, low-risk route. A map-reading exercise alone is not enough preparation for remote or hazardous terrain.

name: Use a compass and orient a map
description: Orient a map to the surrounding terrain and use a compass to determine a direction or bearing on a suitable practice route.

levels.name: Orient the map
levels.completion_criterion: Use visible landmarks and a compass to align a map with the surrounding direction.
levels.can_do: Place map north and the environment in a consistent relationship.

levels.name: Follow a simple bearing
levels.completion_criterion: Identify a direction between two mapped points and follow it on a clear, low-risk practice route.
levels.can_do: Use a compass direction together with mapped features.

levels.name: Account for map and compass details
levels.completion_criterion: Explain when declination matters for the map and region and check the direction against visible terrain features.
levels.can_do: Use bearings thoughtfully and identify sources of navigation error.

emoji_rationale: A magnet represents magnetic direction and compass work.
safety_notes: Practise in a familiar, low-risk area and carry suitable backup navigation. Do not rely on a single compass exercise for remote travel.

name: Choose routes in orienteering
description: Compare possible routes between mapped checkpoints, balancing distance, terrain, path features and the likelihood of navigating accurately.

levels.name: Choose a simple route
levels.completion_criterion: Choose a route along clear paths between two controls and explain the main landmarks you expect to use.
levels.can_do: Make a basic route choice using map features.

levels.name: Compare alternatives
levels.completion_criterion: Compare two feasible routes using distance, terrain and navigation difficulty, then justify your choice.
levels.can_do: Balance speed and navigational certainty.

levels.name: Review a completed course
levels.completion_criterion: After a beginner course, compare planned and actual route choices and identify one decision to improve.
levels.can_do: Learn from route outcomes rather than judging by speed alone.

emoji_rationale: A checkpoint flag represents choosing and completing a route between controls.
safety_notes: Use a beginner course and follow event or land-access rules. Avoid unsafe shortcuts, cliffs, waterways or restricted areas.

name: Classify wildlife camera images
description: Classify camera-trap or trail-camera images according to a project’s stated rules, and record uncertainty instead of forcing a guess.

levels.name: Apply a simple label scheme
levels.completion_criterion: Classify a small set of images using the project’s examples and allowed categories.
levels.can_do: Apply given classification rules consistently.

levels.name: Handle ambiguous images
levels.completion_criterion: Use visible evidence to distinguish similar cases and mark unclear images as uncertain when allowed.
levels.can_do: Avoid overstating what a low-quality image shows.

levels.name: Maintain consistent classifications
levels.completion_criterion: Review a varied batch, compare difficult cases with project guidance and explain the basis for uncertain labels.
levels.can_do: Contribute data consistently while respecting project protocols.

emoji_rationale: Tracks represent identifying and documenting wildlife observations.

name: Georeference collection records
description: Match a locality description in a museum or specimen record to a plausible place on a map, retaining uncertainty when the location cannot be determined reliably.

levels.name: Match an unambiguous locality
levels.completion_criterion: Find a clearly stated locality on a map and record the chosen place according to the project’s instructions.
levels.can_do: Connect place descriptions to a mapped location.

levels.name: Compare possible matches
levels.completion_criterion: Compare names, historical spellings and nearby geographic clues when more than one place seems possible.
levels.can_do: Use evidence to narrow possible locations.

levels.name: Document uncertainty
levels.completion_criterion: Record why a match is preferred and flag ambiguous or insufficient evidence instead of inventing precision.
levels.can_do: Preserve uncertainty and make geographic data reviewable.

emoji_rationale: A map pin represents connecting a written locality to a mapped location.

name: Transcribe historical letters carefully
description: Turn a historical handwritten letter into a faithful text record while preserving meaningful punctuation and marking uncertain words or characters.

levels.name: Transcribe a short clear passage
levels.completion_criterion: Type a short legible passage and compare it line by line with the image.
levels.can_do: Convert handwritten text into a checkable transcription.

levels.name: Handle difficult handwriting
levels.completion_criterion: Preserve original spelling where instructed and mark unclear characters rather than silently modernising them.
levels.can_do: Distinguish what is visible from what is inferred.

levels.name: Review a complete document
levels.completion_criterion: Recheck a longer transcription, follow the project’s conventions and record unresolved readings consistently.
levels.can_do: Produce a faithful, reviewable transcription.

emoji_rationale: A scroll represents working with historical documents.
safety_notes: Follow the project’s privacy and handling rules; use only documents that are appropriate to access and transcribe.

name: Inspect astronomical images systematically
description: Describe visible features in a telescope image and record its context and limitations without claiming scientific conclusions that the image alone cannot support.

levels.name: Describe an image accurately
levels.completion_criterion: Record the visible object or feature and distinguish description from an inference about its cause.
levels.can_do: Describe what an astronomical image visibly shows.

levels.name: Compare images carefully
levels.completion_criterion: Compare two images using their available context and identify visible similarities or differences without assuming the capture conditions are identical.
levels.can_do: Make a structured image comparison.

levels.name: Write a cautious observation note
levels.completion_criterion: Prepare a note listing the image context, observed features, uncertainty and the additional data needed to test an interpretation.
levels.can_do: Document image analysis with appropriate limits.

emoji_rationale: A planet represents examining images of astronomical objects.
safety_notes: Never view the Sun through optical equipment without purpose-built solar filters and appropriate safety guidance; this skill does not teach solar observing.
